description:
Two PRODUCTION sites order work by `format!("{:?}")` over a structure that
embeds a raw interned `Ty`, and that numbering is measured run-unstable.

    product_drive.rs:138  waits.sort_by_cached_key(|wait| format!("{wait:?}"))
    drive.rs:486          unresolved.sort_by_cached_key(|w| format!("{:?}", w.fact.fact()))

`PullWait::Product(RuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey{ activation: ActivationKey{
arrow: Ty }, .. }))` and `FactKey::Activation(ActivationKey{ arrow: Ty })` both
carry a bare arena index.

## The comment at product_drive.rs:131-137 is wrong

It claims the Debug text is "pure data (ids and enum tags, no addresses or
hashes), so sorting by it is a valid, deterministic total order". Measured on
00420_enum_take_drop_split across 4 processes: the arena is renumbered run to
run (16 differing slots in 4 clusters -- see fz-kdt.47, fz-kdt.48). The same
comment also states this order "decides which fact's producer job actually runs
first, which can flip a keep-first merge downstream", so it is load-bearing.
`StableSortKey`'s own doc (`semantic.rs:629-637`) states the opposite of the
comment and is the one that is right.

## The codebase already contradicts itself here

`world.rs:497`, on the set `drive.rs:486` is about to poke producers for:

    /// Order carries no meaning -- demanding producers is commutative -- so no
    /// sort applies.

`drive.rs:486` sorts before doing exactly that. Same operation, opposite
conclusions, ~10 lines apart in effect.

## No divergence observed -- this is a latent hazard, not a live bug

Across 3 runs of the target fixture: program output byte-identical, and the full
public work SEQUENCE (event name + kind + job kind, 17,574 events) byte-identical
-- not merely the multiset. So today the unstable key does not flip anything
observable. It cannot be verified further than this until fz-kdt.34 puts job
IDENTITY in the log rather than job kind; the current log cannot distinguish
"identical work" from "identical kind-sequence with permuted identities".

## The fix is deletion, not a better key

Do NOT repoint these at a canonical rendering. A sort here is a barrier
compensating for an order-sensitive loop, and fz-f98.21's canonical form is
comparison-only and must not enter a production path. If poking producers is
commutative (world.rs:497 says it is), `drive.rs:486` needs no order at all. If
the pull loop's outcome depends on wait processing order, THAT is the defect --
fix the order-sensitivity, then delete the sort.

Same principle as fz-kdt.47 ("determinism comes from canonical data, not a
sorting barrier or scheduler order") applied at a different site; kept separate
because it is a different loop and fz-kdt.47 is already scoped to runtime-demand
derivation.

## Checks

- Both sorts are gone.
- A test drives the pull loop with waits presented in several explicit orders and
  asserts identical settled products and backend output.
- The `world.rs:497` commutativity claim is either proven by test or corrected.
- Correct `product_drive.rs:131-137`'s comment as part of whichever change lands.
title: Delete two compensating Debug-text sorts in the drive/pull loops; make the loops order-insensitive
